item.title: Tracking lightning-induced mangrove canopy gaps in Panama using multi-temporal remote sensing
item.dc:title: Tracking lightning-induced mangrove canopy gaps in Panama using multi-temporal remote sensing
item.dc:creator: Jing Miao Le Wang Wayne P. Sousa a Department of Geography, University at Buffalo, State University of New York, Buffalo, NY, USAb Department of Integrative Biology, University of California, Berkeley, CA, USAJing Miao received the B.E. degree in Surveying and Mapping Engineering from Shandong Agricultural University in 2020, the M.S. degree in Geo-information and Smart City from Shenzhen University in 2023, and she is currently pursuing her PhD degree in Geography at the University at Buffalo. Her research interests are mangrove forest dynamics and coastal resilience through remote sensing and spatial analysis.Le Wang received the B.E. degree from the Wuhan Technical University of Surveying and Mapping in 1996, the M.S. degree from Peking University in 1999, and the Ph.D. degree in environmental science, policy, and management from the University of California at Berkeley in 2003. He is currently a Professor and Chair of Geography at The State University of New York. He has authored or coauthored more than 110 refereed journal articles, which have been cited 10,000 times on Google Scholar. His work has been funded by NSF, USDA, and USGS. His research interests focus on remote sensing of coastal mangrove forests, invasive species, and urban environments.Wayne P. Sousa received the B.S. degree in zoology from the University of Rhode Island in 1973 and the M.A. and Ph.D. degrees in biological sciences from the University of California, Santa Barbara, in 1975 and 1977, respectively. He is currently a Professor Emeritus in the Department of Integrative Biology at the University of California, Berkeley. His research interests include community ecology, with a particular emphasis on ecological disturbances, mangrove forest dynamics, and host–parasite interactions.

item.title: Carbon sink potential and evolution of vegetation suitable zones in China during the dual-carbon period (2020–2060)
item.dc:title: Carbon sink potential and evolution of vegetation suitable zones in China during the dual-carbon period (2020–2060)
item.dc:creator: Jiayun Niu Wei Gong Shuo Shi Jinyang Wu Minghui Wu Xingtao Tang Zixi Shi Chenxi Liu a Electronic Information School, Wuhan University, Wuhan, Chinab State Key Laboratory of Information Engineering in Surveying, Mapping and Remote Sensing, Wuhan University, Wuhan, Chinac Perception and Effectiveness Assessment for Carbon-Neutrality Efforts, Engineering Research Center of Ministry of Education, Wuhan, ChinaJiayun Niu received a B.E. degree in Surveying and Mapping Engineering from Shandong Jianzhu University in 2020. In 2024, she received a Master’s degree from China University of Geosciences (Wuhan). She is currently pursuing a Ph.D. at the School of Electronics and Information Technology, Wuhan University. Her research interests include lidar, vegetation carbon storage monitoring, and new energy.Wei Gong received the B.S. degree in photonics engineering from the Huazhong University of Science and Technology (HUST) in 1993, the M.S. degree in electronics from the Chinese Academy of Sciences in 1996, and the Ph.D. degree in physical electronics from HUST in 1999. From 2002 to 2004, he served as an Assistant Professor with Hampton University, Hampton. He is mainly engaged in teaching and research of new lasers, optical technology, and its remote sensing applications, and has made achievements in atmospheric LiDAR and optical remote sensing.Shuo Shi received the Ph.D. degree in photogrammetry and remote sensing from Wuhan University in 2015. He is currently a Professor with the State Key Laboratory of Information Engineering in Surveying, Mapping and Remote Sensing (LIESMARS), Wuhan University. He has authored over 30 peer-reviewed research articles. His research interests include hyperspectral LiDAR, fluorescence LiDAR, true-color imaging, target classification, and vegetation quantitative remote sensing.Jinyang Wu is a doctoral student at the State Key Laboratory of Information Engineering in Surveying, Mapping and Remote Sensing (LIESMARS), Wuhan University. Her research interests focus on the study of aerosols and trace gases, radiative transfer, and atmospheric pollutant chemical processes based on ground-based observations and satellite remote sensing.Minghui Wu received a B.E. degree in Surveying and Mapping Engineering and a B.A. in English (Double Degree) from Linyi University in 2021. She then earned her master’s degree in Surveying and Mapping Engineering from China University of Geosciences in 2024, which included a joint training period at the Wuhan Botanical Garden, Chinese Academy of Sciences. She has been pursuing her Ph.D. at the State Key Laboratory of Information Engineering in Surveying, Mapping and Remote Sensing since 2024. Her research interests include lidar data processing and applications, as well as forest carbon sequestration monitoring and mapping.Xingtao Tang received the B.S. degree in measurement and control technology and instrumentation from the School of Mechanical and Electronic Engineering, Wuhan University of Technology, in 2020. He received his master’s degree from the State Key Laboratory of Surveying, Mapping and Remote Sensing Information Engineering, Wuhan University, in 2024. He’s currently pursuing his doctorate at Wuhan University’s School of Electronics and Information Technology. His research interests include hyperspectral LiDAR data processing, point cloud classification, and vegetation carbon storage monitoring.Zixi Shi received the B.E. degree from China University of Geosciences, China, in 2021. She is currently pursuing the Ph.D. degree with the State Key Laboratory of Information Engineering in Surveying, Mapping and Remote Sensing, Wuhan University. Her research interests include quantitative remote sensing inversion, LiDAR data processing, and multi-source remote sensing data fusion.Chenxi Liu received the M.S. degree in Geological Engineering (Geographic Information Engineering) from Yangtze University in 2022. She is currently pursuing a Ph.D. degree at Wuhan University. Her primary research interests include forest parameter inversion using spaceborne LiDAR, the fusion of multisource satellite images, large-scale ecological remote sensing data analysis, and machine learning algorithms.
